public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim is that paying demand in 2024 was too small to cover the cost of generative AI. He concedes the tools have some fit. Evidence for 2024 bears this out. OpenAI, the clear market leader, expected about a $5 billion loss on $3.7 billion of revenue and was raising new outside money. In June 2024 Sequoia's David Cahn estimated a roughly $500 billion gap between AI infrastructure spending and the revenue needed to justify it. ChatGPT's usage doubled to 200 million weekly users, so demand was real and growing, but that does not show revenue covering costs. The outcome depends on reading 'scale necessary to support its existence' as revenue covering costs.
limitations: The claim has no stated threshold; the result depends on the revenue-covers-costs reading.
The Sequoia figure is an investor's estimate, not measured data.
Later revenue growth after 2024 is outside the period tested.
